bib.title: The Perils & Promises of Fact-checking with Large Language Models

question: How well do GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 fact-check claims, with and without agent-driven web-search context, and across languages?
hypothesis: Retrieved context improves LLM fact-checking accuracy, and GPT-4 outperforms GPT-3.5 (implied by the design).
contributions: Evaluation of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 on fact-checking with and without external context
A ReAct-based iterative agent that queries Google, explains its reasoning and cites retrieved sources
First assessment of GPT-3.5 fact-checking across multiple languages

method.summary: A LangChain ReAct agent lets GPT-3.5 or GPT-4 issue Google search queries (up to three iterations, 10 results each, previews only) before giving a verdict; fact-checking domains are filtered from results. It is compared with a no-context prompt on PolitiFact claims and, for GPT-3.5, on multilingual Data Commons claims in original language versus English translation.
method.task: claim veracity classification with evidence retrieval

datasets.name: PolitiFact fact-checks
datasets.split: 500 per label across six labels (True, Mostly-True, Half-True, Mostly-False, False, Pants-Fire)

datasets.name: Data Commons fact-check dump
datasets.size: 78 languages, 454 organisations; up to 500 per language kept
datasets.split: languages with >=50 observations and >=10 true/mostly-true kept
datasets.preprocessing: Verdicts translated to English, 468 verdicts appearing at least twice mapped by hand to 4 levels (False, Mostly False, Mostly True, True); unmappable (Sarcasm, Satire, unconfirmed) removed; claims translated to English with Googletrans

models.name: GPT-4
models.context: 16k (stated as the standard GPT API window; applied to both)

inference.samples: one run per claim; no seeds or repeats stated
inference.prompting: No Context: statement, originator and date; model may answer 'uncertain'. Context: ReAct agent in LangChain, may issue Google queries or answer.
inference.retrieval: Google Search API, 10 results per iteration, previews (title, link, snippet); results from fact-checking domains in the dataset removed

parameters.max_search_iterations: 3 (then forced final answer from all searches)

metrics.name: Accuracy (binary)
metrics.definition: PolitiFact labels grouped into false (pants-fire, false, mostly-false) and true (half-true, mostly-true, true); correct if grouped category matches

metrics.name: Accuracy (exact six-way)
metrics.definition: correct only if exact PolitiFact category predicted

metrics.name: Accuracy and F1 (multilingual)
metrics.definition: 4-level verdict mapped scores; F1 added because class distribution differs by language

eval.protocol: F1 confidence intervals are bootstrapped standard errors (Fig 7); 'significant' differences asserted without a named test; time analysis against the Sept 2021 cutoff.

availability.code: not stated; LangChain library cited; full transcripts said to be in supplementary material
availability.data: PolitiFact and Data Commons datasets (public sources)

results.claim: With context, non-ambiguous verdicts reach above 80% and 89% accuracy; without context 63-75% average accuracy.
results.setup: PolitiFact, 3000 claims (500 per six-way label), GPT-3.5 / GPT-4 via ReAct Google-search agent (Context) or plain prompt (No Context)
results.quote:
demon-
strate good performance of 63-75% accuracy on average, which further improves to above 80% and 89%
for non-ambiguous verdicts when context is incorporated

results.claim: GPT-4 with context reaches 84.92% on 'true' claims versus 71.30% without context (binary accuracy).
results.table: Table 1 left, row true, columns GPT-4 Context (84.92) vs GPT-4 No Context (71.30)

results.claim: GPT-3.5 without context predicts false in 58.2% of cases versus 22.89% for GPT-4.
results.quote:
GPT-3.5 predicts the veracity of a claim to be false in 58.2% of the cases (compared to 22.89%
for GPT-4)

results.claim: Context raises GPT-4's accuracy on true-label categories by 10.19 points on average.
results.setup: PolitiFact, GPT-4 true categories, context vs no context
results.quote: where it achieves an increase of 10.19 percentage points on average

results.claim: Both models fall in the middle categories: GPT-4 with context gets 55.82% on mostly-false, below its 68.70% without context.
results.table: Table 1 left, row mostly false, GPT-4 Context vs No Context

results.claim: Exact six-way accuracy is very low: the authors say models cannot predict the exact shade of truth.
results.setup: PolitiFact, both models, both conditions, exact-category accuracy
results.quote:
The extremely low scores show that the models are unable to predict the exact shade of
truth that PolitiFact assigned to the statement.

results.claim: No sudden accuracy drop after the September 2021 training cutoff, interpreted as RLHF possibly adding knowledge.
results.quote:
We do not observe any sudden decrease in accuracy after the
official training cutoff for GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.

results.claim: Translating non-English claims to English raised F1 in all languages except Thai without context.
results.setup: Data Commons multilingual fact-checks, GPT-3.5, up to 500 claims per language, 13 languages besides English, no context
results.quote:
In all languages, except for Thai, we see an increase in the F1 score of the model when fact-checking the
translated claim as compared to the original.

results.claim: With context, translation raised F1 in all but three languages (Portuguese, Thai, Italian).
results.setup: Data Commons multilingual fact-checks, GPT-3.5, up to 500 claims per language, 13 languages besides English, with context
results.quote:
In all but three languages (Portugese, Thai, and Italian), translating increased the
F1 score of the model.

results.claim: Telugu without context: accuracy 26.99 on original-language claims versus 59.79 on English translation.
results.setup: Telugu, GPT-3.5, no context, 500 samples; baseline is English translation
results.table: Table 2, row Telugu, columns Accuracy Multilingual (26.99) and Accuracy English (59.79)

results.claim: Tamil with context: F1 62.95 English versus 34.86 original.
results.table: Table 3, row Tamil, columns F1 Multilingual (34.86), F1 English (62.95)

results.claim: BM25 distillation of full web pages gave no improvement over Google result previews.
results.quote:
We found no
improvement to the performance of the LLMs,
as Google already uses machine learning methods

limits: No exact model versions, temperature, decoding settings or prompts printed; single run, no seeds.
Data leakage of fact-checks into training data cannot be excluded; the cutoff test is indirect.
Cross-language comparison is confounded: fact-checking organisations differ in topics and timeliness, so low-resource languages may do better than reported.
Only GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 tested; authors note newer, possibly fine-tuned models.
Models cannot replace human fact-checkers; wrong verdicts can be costly.
Retrieval relies on Google previews and assumes retrieved information is trustworthy; Google also differs by language and date.
'Significant' is stated without naming a test; the PolitiFact accuracy tables do not include variance.
16k context limited how much search content could be passed.
